steps.content: You leave the cargo hold and head down the corridor toward the boiler room, searching for any sign of her.
Fog is everywhere. The faint blue glow from your earring is the only light you have. You wade alone through the flooded passages, calling her name again and again.
The only answer is the sound of distant waves.
[Black Screen Transition]
Hope slowly dies in the cold seawater.
You wander through a maze of passages, past one empty room after another, searching every dark corner.
Your throat is hoarse; you can't manage another sound. The fog corrodes what's left of your mind, leaving only a numb, hollow shell.
In the end, only instinct drives you onward in mechanical, meaningless repetition, searching the endless dark for a companion who no longer exists.
The blue light hasn't flickered in a very long time.
[Black Screen Transition]
An unknown obsession has taken root in your heart.
You can no longer hear Schorl, but you don't feel lost. The Abyss extends into a vast emptiness, echoing with nothing but your own persistence.
In your absurdly long search, you finally begin to realize that <color=#fb9259>you are going down</color>.
The passages and cabins from your memory are stretched, twisted, and reassembled, merging together in grotesque ways. No matter how far you walk, you can't find an exit back to the upper decks.
<color=#fb9259>You are heading into the Abyss.</color>
Your legs have soaked in seawater for so long that they've grown swollen and heavy, like rotting wood in a swamp that could crumble at any moment.
Then, your body begins to rot. Your spine can barely support your weight, and you tumble to the ground.
Cold seawater flows over you, dissolving your body and consciousness. Soon, you'll melt into a puddle of shapeless ichor, just like...
Just like what happened to them. To your companions.
Are you going to give up here?
Your fists furiously slam into the ground, the pain bringing your mind back to clarity as the bodily hallucinations recede like a tide.
Just as Shin said, the source of it all is down there. How could you possibly run? Even if it means death, you have to face the truth.
The fog has lifted without you noticing, and a pale gray figure stands at a corner not far away. You can't make out her face, but her silhouette and voice feel achingly familiar.
Well done, child... You have managed to overcome despair.
I believe you can reach the deeper truths.
She disappears at the end of the passage.
You snap back to consciousness. Scrambling through the water, you chase after her.
